title: The Dog the Soviets Left to Die in Orbit

scenes.voiceover: For five months, a dead dog kept circling the Earth. Her name was Laika, and she was never meant to come home.
scenes.mainText: A DEAD DOG ORBITED EARTH FOR 5 MONTHS
scenes.visualConcept: The iconic real Laika portrait, slow push in.

scenes.voiceover: In 1957 she was a stray pulled off the streets of Moscow, chosen because a stray had already survived hunger and cold.
scenes.mainText: A MOSCOW STRAY, CHOSEN TO SURVIVE

scenes.voiceover: Here is the part that still unsettles people. Sputnik 2 had no way to come back. No parachute. No plan. From the moment she was sealed in, it was one way.
scenes.mainText: THERE WAS NO WAY HOME. BY DESIGN.

scenes.voiceover: The cabin overheated within hours, and Laika died from the heat and stress. But the Soviet Union said she passed peacefully after days, and hid the truth for forty five years.
scenes.mainText: DEAD IN HOURS. THE LIE LASTED 45 YEARS.

scenes.voiceover: One of the scientists who prepared her said it plainly, decades later. We did not learn enough from this mission to justify the death of the dog.
scenes.mainText: "WE DID NOT LEARN ENOUGH TO JUSTIFY IT."
scenes.visualConcept: Laika portrait again, the loop back.

scenes.voiceover: She was the first. She was not the last. Every animal we sent to space is on the channel.
scenes.mainText: SHE WASN'T THE LAST → ON THE CHANNEL
